# `transform` dialect

CEIR-27 sec-71/sec-72/sec-146 the transform dialect: an AUTHORABLE optimization-SCHEDULE program. A transform module is a SEPARATE asset (NOT the payload) whose directive ops set program-global compilation knobs the payload program is then planned with -- so two schedules optimize ONE semantic program (sec-146). This slice (27a) ships the two PROGRAM-GLOBAL knobs the tensor pipeline already exposes as PlanOptions (fuse_gemm_relu, share_intermediate_storage), hoisting the C++ struct into an authored asset (the tensor_pipeline.hpp 26f/27 'fusion IS a schedule decision' seed). The ceir-gpu loader plan_options_from_transform walks the module and maps each directive to its PlanOptions field; an ABSENT directive keeps the base default (a partial schedule is legal). Per-op TARGETING (sec-71 fine-grained 'fuse THESE ops' via payload handles/matchers) is NAMED-FORWARD: it lands when a corpus has two fusable sites wanting DIFFERENT decisions (no live consumer today -- both knobs are program-global by construction, the 26b-4 no-speculative rule). Declarative rewrite RULES (sec-72) are 27c. Directive ops carry NO results/operands and NO effects (compile-time schedule metadata, not runtime work) and are NOT Pure -- a directive is NOT a value computation, so Pure/CSE/DCE reasoning does not apply, and marking it Pure would be a CATEGORY ERROR (two structurally-identical directives, e.g. two transform.fuse{true}, would become CSE merge candidates). A transform module is read by the loader and DISCARDED -- no pass ever runs on it. Module-wide well-formedness (a program-global knob set at most ONCE) is the SEPARATE walk transform::find_transform_misuse (the find_resource/quant_misuse house pattern): a second occurrence of a directive is DuplicateDirective; the generated verify_fuse/verify_share_storage own the STRUCTURAL contract (the required bool enable). CEIR-29a-3b ADDS a THIRD program-global directive, transform.assign_provider (a required string `provider`): it PINS the ml-op partitioner (partition_ml, ceir-gpu) to a named execution provider -- the ceir-gpu loader provider_from_transform resolves the name to an MlProvider span index partition_ml honours as a PREFERENCE. find_transform_misuse gains seen_assign (a duplicate assign_provider is DuplicateDirective, same as fuse/share). CEIR-29c-3b ADDS a FOURTH directive, transform.constrain_provider_class (a required string `class`): it CONSTRAINS the partitioner to a provider CLASS (host/gpu/npu/media/external) as a HARD FILTER (a sec-102 portability boundary, unlike assign_provider's preference) -- the ceir-gpu loader constraint_from_transform resolves the name to a ProviderClass partition_ml filters by; it COMPOSES with assign_provider (filter outer, pin inner). find_transform_misuse gains seen_constrain (a duplicate is DuplicateDirective).
